params.place: a phone on a dark desk, its screen sliding off to show the chip

moments.what: the phone's screen slides away, its board and main chip glowing
the camera pushes down onto the chip, its lid lifting off
the die underneath lights up
a wave of light ripples across the die
the die flares, the camera close over it

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: Every chip you own is built from a Bell Labs invention.

params.place: deep in the chip: a city of tiny glowing switches

moments.what: a field of tiny switches, one glowing amber, a label writes on
the field dims around the one amber switch
a question mark of light rises over it
the camera pulls back, the question mark pulsing

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: The transistor. What did the very first one look like?

params.place: Bell Labs, a winter lab bench under a desk lamp

moments.what: the lab bench lights up under the lamp, the year on the wall calendar
a Bell Labs sign lights on the wall
the lamp brightens over the bench
a name plate for John Bardeen slides out on the bench
a second plate for Walter Brattain slides out beside it
tweezers, a razor and a gold foil roll roll onto the bench
close on the tweezers lifting a strip of gold foil

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: In 1947, John Bardeen and Walter Brattain built it by hand.

params.place: close on the bench: a clear plastic triangle on a stand

moments.what: the gold foil strip lifts and curls toward the plastic triangle
the foil wraps over the triangle's point and down both faces
the clear plastic wedge catches the lamp light, a label writes on
a razor blade swings in over the tip
the camera dives to the tip of the wedge
the foil folds over the point of the wedge
the blade cuts a hairline slit; the gold splits into two strips

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: Brattain wrapped gold foil around a plastic wedge and slit it at the tip with a razor.

params.place: the test stand: a spring arm over a grey germanium crystal on a metal base

moments.what: the two gold strips at the tip glow, a label writes on for each
a tiny gap between them flashes
a bracket marks the gap
a bent wire spring flexes and pushes the wedge down
the wedge lowers onto the crystal
the grey germanium slab lights where the gold meets it, its label writes on
a spark flashes where the gold touches the crystal
a question mark of light pulses between the two contacts
the question mark swells

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: Two gold contacts, almost touching, pressed by a spring onto germanium. So how does that do anything?

params.place: inside the germanium, cut open under the two contacts

moments.what: the crystal slices open; a small cyan wave pulses on the left wire
a voltage meter's needle on the left wire swings
the left contact glows in time with the wave
the amber current under the right contact swells and shrinks with it
the amber stream through the crystal pulses, the camera pulls back
the stream runs down into the metal base
the right contact flares on each swell

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: A small voltage on one contact controls the current through the other.

params.place: an oscilloscope on the lab shelf, its round screen glowing green

moments.what: the scope's screen warms up on the shelf, a calendar page on the shelf flips
a small wiggle crawls across the screen
the wiggle travels down a wire into the wedge
a tall wave bursts out on the second trace
the tall wave doubles in height and the wedge flashes
the gain plate on the scope lights and starts counting
the scope's screen brightens green
the gain figure counts up on the scope's dial plate

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: On December sixteenth, a weak signal came out up to 100 times stronger.

params.place: a dark bench, the transistor wired to a lamp

moments.what: the camera swings to the transistor wired to a dark bulb
the bulb's filament glints
the transistor's contacts glow
the bulb flickers
a toggle in the signal wire clicks
a small pulse runs into the contact
the big current lights the bulb
the bulb blazes
the pulse stops and the bulb goes dark

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: Why does it matter? The same trick is a switch: a small signal turns a big current on or off.

params.place: a graphics card on a dark stage, dived into its chip

moments.what: the transistor shrinks to a glowing dot
the dot copies into rows, then a field of thousands
the field pulls back into a die; a graphics card fades up around it
the chip's generation name writes on under the card's name
the field's edges snap into a square
the card's fans spin
the chip's die glows on the open card
the camera dives back into the die, a wave of light sweeping the switches, the count climbing on it
the count starts climbing on the die
a second wave of light sweeps the switches
the count lands and the whole die flares

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: Shrink it, copy it, and one NVIDIA Ada Lovelace graphics chip holds up to 76B of them.

params.place: the phone on the dark desk again

moments.what: the gold wedge stands small and glowing
the wedge turns, its gold catching the light
the wedge flashes and sinks into the chip
the chip settles onto a phone's board
the phone's back slides closed
the chip's die glows under the wedge
the camera settles on the opening shot of the phone

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: All from gold foil on a plastic wedge: the switch now inside every chip in your phone.
